Services.title: Our services

House.intro: A great house that makes no garments: what it composes is presence. It chooses, it introduces, then it keeps watch.

sections.title: Our story
sections.text: Maison Triona was born of a lifetime spent alongside families. After many years of arranging companionship on behalf of others, Catriona is opening a house of her own, under her name and to her standards.

sections.title: Our standards
sections.text: We choose each person one by one, for their skill and for their bearing. We introduce only people we would trust with our own family.

sections.title: Discretion
sections.text: No social media: the house lives by recommendation. Nothing a family entrusts to us leaves the house without their agreement.

sections.title: The meaning of the name
sections.text: Triona comes from the founder’s first name, a name that means “pure”. Her family name means “the navigator in a dugout canoe”: the house’s seal draws a T that opens out like a wake on the water. You never see the navigator, only the trace they leave behind. That is how we work. The K. is her signature, always small and set back: a mark, not a second name.

sections.title: Experience
sections.text: Thirty years of orchestrating, in silence. Thirty years of coordinating companionship at home, before opening this house.

countries.text: Discretion is a way of life here; it is ours too.

sections.title: When you write to us
paragraphs: To reply to you, the form asks for:
items: The service you are interested in and, if you wish, who it is for.
The country concerned.
Whether the enquiry is urgent.
Your name, and an email address or a telephone number.
When and in which language you would prefer us to contact you.
A message, if you wish.
How you heard of the house, if you would like to say.
after: This information is used to reply to you and, if you wish, to introduce you to one or more people. How you heard of the house is used only to know where enquiries come from.
The service, the country, the urgency, your name, an email address or a telephone number, the language and your consent are needed to reply to you; everything else is optional.
There is no need to share any medical details; we will talk about it in person.
If you choose to meet a professional, we pass on to them, with your consent, your name, your contact details and what is useful to them about your situation.
If you give an email address, you receive a short confirmation. It repeats nothing of your enquiry.
No decision is made by automated means: every enquiry is read by a person.

sections.title: When you arrange a call
paragraphs: You may also arrange a call with us. The house sends you a personal link, valid for 48 hours, to choose your time; no account or cookie is needed.

To receive this link, you give us your email address. It is used only to send it to you: our email provider receives it and keeps a record of it for as long as our sending domain is active. We do not keep it; only a fingerprint, which does not reveal it, stays with the link for a few days, to cancel an earlier link and to limit repeated requests (three a day at most).
We then keep your name, your number, the language and time you chose and, if you wish to say, how you heard of the house. We never leave a voicemail.

This information is encrypted as soon as it arrives, like an enquiry: only the house can read it. Only the time and the status of the call remain readable, so that the same time is never offered twice.
Once the call is arranged, the page offers you a file to add to your calendar; it contains neither your name nor your number.

sections.title: How your enquiries are protected
items: The content of your enquiry (your name, contact details, preferred time, who it is for and your message) is encrypted as soon as it reaches our server, then stored in a vault hosted in the European Union.
So that we can sort enquiries, a few details remain readable in the vault: the service, the country, the language, the urgency, the source and the dates.

Only two people can read the encrypted content: the founder of the house and the person in charge of the technical upkeep of the site. Every login requires two-factor authentication; every reading, export or deletion is recorded in a log.
The message that tells us a new enquiry has arrived contains nothing of your enquiry: only its date and a link to the vault.

Our technical logs keep nothing you write: only an identifier and the outcome of the submission. As for any website, our host records the address of the pages visited, the date, your IP address and your browser, for one day.
To block abusive submissions, we keep for 24 hours at most a fingerprint of your IP address, computed with a key changed every day, and a fingerprint of the confirmation address.

sections.title: Our correspondence, afterwards
paragraphs: Once we are in touch, we reply by email or by telephone. Our email correspondence is kept in the house mailbox, hosted by [À DÉFINIR], for as long as we work together, then [À DÉFINIR].

sections.title: What we measure
paragraphs: To know whether the site is useful, we count page views and a few choices, such as the service viewed, always as totals. The tool we use, Plausible, sets no cookies. To count visitors without identifying them, it computes a daily fingerprint from your IP address and your browser, with a key erased every 24 hours; your IP address is not kept, only the country, region and city are derived from it. It is served from our own domain; its data is hosted in Germany.

sections.title: Cookies and storage in your browser
paragraphs: This site sets no cookies. The language is shown in the address of the page.

During your visit, and only for as long as it lasts, your browser may keep three things: the fact that you closed the language suggestion, the fact that you paused the videos, and the choices already made for your enquiry (service, country, language, time), so that they are not lost from one page or step to the next. Who the enquiry is for, your name, contact details, message and urgency are never kept there. Everything disappears when you close the tab; the choices for your enquiry are also erased when you send it.

sections.title: Our technical providers
paragraphs: A few providers keep the site running. Each is bound to the house by a data processing agreement and uses your information only for the service it provides.

facts.value: Hosting of the site. The functions that receive your enquiry run in Paris.
Enquiry vault and sending of emails, in France.
Protection against abusive submissions, on servers located in the European Union.
Audience measurement as totals, without cookies; data hosted in Germany.

sections.title: Outside the European Union
paragraphs: Vercel and Upstash are American companies: even when processed on European servers, data may be accessible from the United States.

sections.title: How long we keep your information
items: Your enquiry: for as long as we are in touch, then it is erased. You may ask us to erase it sooner.
Your call: the same length of time as an enquiry. Personal links are erased two days after they expire, or after the call they were used to arrange.
Backups: an erased enquiry may remain there for 7 days before it disappears; its content stays encrypted.
Our host’s logs: one day.
Protection against abusive submissions: 24 hours at most.
Email sending logs: [À CONFIRMER selon le fournisseur]
The vault access log: [À DÉFINIR]
Our email correspondence: [À DÉFINIR]

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: At any time, you may see the information we hold about you, have it corrected or erased, object to its processing, restrict its use, receive a copy of it in a common format or have it passed to someone else, and withdraw your consent; withdrawing it does not affect what was done before. Write to us at [CONTENT TO BE PROVIDED BY CAT]; we will reply within one month.
You may also, at any time, lodge a complaint with the data protection authority of your country. Our supervisory authority is the Data Protection Authority in Belgium.
items: Belgium: Data Protection Authority (APD).
France: Commission nationale de l’informatique et des libertés (CNIL).
Luxembourg: National Commission for Data Protection (CNPD).
Monaco: Personal Data Protection Authority (APDP).
Switzerland: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).

sections.title: The limits we know of
paragraphs: No system is perfect. Here are the limits we know of, and would rather tell you about:
items: Our host, Vercel, is an American company. Your enquiry passes through its servers in readable form until it is encrypted; we do not store it there. Like any American company, Vercel may be required by American law to hand over data, even data processed in Europe.
An erased enquiry remains in the backups for up to 7 days; its content stays encrypted.
The personal booking link appears in our host’s logs. It is only valid for 48 hours; once the call is arranged, it only serves to see the confirmation again, until the call.
The confirmation is sent to the address typed into the form. If it reaches you although you did not write to us, please ignore it: it contains nothing but an acknowledgement of receipt.

sections.title: If an incident occurs
paragraphs: If an incident affected your information, we would inform the data protection authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of it and, if the risk were high, the people concerned.

sections.title: If this policy changes
paragraphs: The new version is published on this page, with its date.

Faq.title: Common questions
Faq.intro: What you may be wondering before you write to us, and our answers.

items.question: Will my information remain confidential?
items.answer: Yes. Everything you entrust to us stays within the house; we pass on to the professional you choose only what is useful to them, with your consent. Your enquiries are kept in an encrypted vault in the European Union, then erased.

items.question: Who pays whom? What will it cost me?
items.answer: You pay nothing to the house. You pay the professional you have chosen directly. The house is paid by them.

items.question: How do you choose the people you introduce?
items.answer: We meet and vet every person before introducing them to you. We look at their skill, but also at their bearing, their discretion and their judgement. We recommend no one we would not trust with our own family.

items.question: What happens if the person is not right for me?
items.answer: Tell us. We adjust, or we introduce you to someone else, without you having to give a reason.

items.question: Which countries do you work in?
items.answer: In Belgium, France, Luxembourg, Monaco and Switzerland. We reply in French or in English.

items.question: How quickly will I hear back?
items.answer: Within 48 working hours, Monday to Friday. We reply to you personally.

items.question: Do I need to share medical information?
items.answer: No. There’s no need to share any medical details; we’ll talk about it in person. For any medical need, we will refer you to the appropriate health professionals.

items.question: Can I make an enquiry for someone close to me?
items.answer: Yes. You can write to us for yourself or for someone close to you. A few lines are enough; we then get to know each other in a first conversation.

Accessibility.title: Accessibility
Accessibility.intro: We want everyone to be able to read this site and write to us, however they browse.

sections.title: Our aim
paragraphs: This site aims for level AA of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.2), and level AAA for the contrast of body text.

sections.title: Where we stand
paragraphs: The site is being prepared. To date, every page has been checked with automated tests and with the keyboard:
items: no errors reported by the axe tool, in French and in English;
a visible marker on the element reached with the keyboard, and touch targets of at least 48 pixels;
every page can be read without JavaScript and without animation;
every video can be paused.

sections.title: What remains to be done
paragraphs: Before opening, the site will be tried with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers, and by people outside the house. The contact form, still being built, will be checked in the same way.

sections.title: Tell us about a difficulty
paragraphs: If a page is difficult for you to read or use, write to us at [CONTENT TO BE PROVIDED BY CAT]. We will give you the information in another form.
